newsitem.title: USA: Ill. nuclear power plant may be fined by commission.
newsitem.headline: Ill. nuclear power plant may be fined by commission.

text.p: The U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission said Friday it proposed a $50,000 fine against Commonwealth Edison Co., a unit of Unicom Corp., for problems at its nuclear plant in Cordova, Ill.
The commission cited "inadequate evaluation and repairs of the interior and exterior siding of the reactor building at the Quad Cities Nuclear Power Station."

In May 1996, the corrugated steel siding of the plant was damaged by high winds. ComEd promptly repaired the interior siding, but put off exterior repairs on the belief that they were only cosmetic, the commission said.

"Both the interior and exterior siding are needed for the reactor building to fill its design function of containing radioactive releases in the unlikely event of a reactor accident," the commission said.
ComEd has until July 24 to pay the fine or protest it. If the fine is protested and the commission formally imposes it, the utility can request a hearing, the commission said.
"We will be reviewing the fine," said Unicom spokesman Gary Wald.

He said that the Quad Cities plant was shut down before the May 1996 storm hit. The interior siding was repaired in June, while exterior panels were not repaired until July, he said. "We agree that we misjudged the importance of that corrugated (exterior) siding," Wald said.
He added, however, that the Quad Cities plant was not returned to service until after both the interior and exterior siding had been repaired.
